clue.text: Author can resist being rewritten

indicators.note: text being rewritten has its letters set down afresh, so the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer is able to hold out against having their work revised by an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenarist writes scenarios or screenplays for films, which makes them a kind of writer.

clue.text: Old boy turns up wearing unfashionable satin shoe

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it around it, so the trimmed satin goes around the other piece
unfashionable means not in, so the letters spelling in are dropped from satin
in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil arrives wearing a dated satin slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfashionable' means not in, so those two letters leave the fabric; 'turns up' suits a down clue, where reading upward reverses; 'wearing' puts the old boy inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog of the kind worn by French peasants, so a type of footwear.

clue.text: D bogarde sworn in as different actor

indicators.note: something made different is changed, so these letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Dirk Bogarde is sworn in as a different film star.
explanation.walkthrough: D BOGARDE suggests Dirk Bogarde, the British film actor, but 'D bogarde sworn in' is all anagram fodder, signalled by 'different'; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood star of gangster pictures such as Little Caesar and Key Largo was a screen performer.

clue.text: But a learner's considered to be wasting time ultimately

parts.note: L stands for learner, from the L-plate shown on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: wasting means losing something, so the letter for time is dropped from the word
ultimately points to the very end of the word, where that letter is lost

parts.note: considered, as in 'it was considered', means thought

explanation.surface: A novice driver is thought to be idling the hours away in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting time ultimately' removes the final T from THOUGHT, leaving THOUGH. 'But' at the start looks like a link word but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions introducing a contrasting clause, a concession set against what went before.

clue.text: Composer takes the plunge, skipping intro

indicators.note: skipping the intro means leaving out the opening letter of the word for diving in

parts.note: takes the plunge, read literally, means dives into water

explanation.surface: A musician finally commits to something, leaving out the opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles of that surname was an American modernist; 'takes the plunge' looks figurative but is literal diving.
explanation.definitionFit: The American modernist Charles of that surname wrote The Unanswered Question, so he was a writer of music.

clue.text: Huge antique set damaged

indicators.note: damaged goods are broken up, so the letters of these two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An old set of furniture or china has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the giant Titans of Greek myth, something so described is colossal in size.

clue.text: Fellow economists backing cut

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the slice from economists is read from right to left
a cut from the word economists is a slice of its letters, the run sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Colleagues in economics support a reduction in spending.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside ecoNOMISts sits NOMIS, which 'backing' turns round; 'cut' marks a piece taken from the word, not a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, and setters let any male name stand for a fellow or chap.

clue.text: Drunk treated thus?

parts.note: thus means so, in this way
treated means used, as in 'treated well' or 'used well'

explanation.surface: Someone handled in this way might well end up tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated thus' reads naturally as one idea, but it splits into two words that, swapped into answer order, spell the definition; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated, as if pickled in brine or liquor.

clue.text: Prominent politician, one times at first rubbished

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the words one times at first are thrown together into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior figure in government was the first to be trashed by the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' and 'at first' look like instructions, but with 'one' they are all anagram fodder for 'rubbished'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British government rank sits just below Cabinet level, a senior post under a department's head.

clue.text: Strict observance of rules under new head? That's to be expected

indicators.note: under a new head means placed beneath a replacement leader, here a changed opening letter
head refers to the top letter of the word, which is the one swapped out

parts.note: formality is rigid adherence to rules, etiquette and convention

explanation.surface: A regime of rigid rules under a new boss? Well, that is predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under new head' swaps the first letter of FORMALITY, its head in a down clue, for N.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the usual, standard state of affairs, which is just what anyone would predict.

clue.text: Policeman identified London marathon participant?

definitions.meaning: an officer of the early London force attached to Henry Fielding's magistrates' court, founded in 1749
jokingly, someone racing along a street in Bow, a district of East London

explanation.surface: A police officer recognised one of the runners in the London Marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fielding's 1749 force, based at a London magistrates' court, was the capital's first professional police; the second reading imagines a racer on that street.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielding's eighteenth-century thief-takers were London's first paid detectives, hence policemen; the second sense is a literal athlete on that road.

clue.text: Person with twenty five? No, presumably

parts.note: flip the two letters of this word and you get the solution's second word; the first word is the instruction to flip them

explanation.surface: Is there anyone with twenty-five of anything? Presumably not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twenty five' refers to 25 across, the allure clue, so the definition is a person with that quality; 'presumably' marks the clue as the result of following the answer's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with allure arouses desire, so to an admirer such a person is an exciting, arousing figure.

clue.text: Protective coat finally removed in salt water

indicators.note: the final letter is taken away, so the coating's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the British name for the bitumen rustproofing sprayed beneath a car body

explanation.surface: Rustproofing on a car is eventually stripped off by seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is the British term for car-underbody rustproofing; 'finally removed' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes things below the ocean surface, that is, submerged in brine.

clue.text: Nothing eaten at first during Lenten rituals, Christian celebrations

parts.note: love means nothing, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: during means within, so that letter sits inside the Lenten observances

parts.note: fasts are the abstentions observed during Lent

indicators.note: at first picks out only the opening letter of the word eaten

explanation.surface: Abstaining from food during Lent, the faithful mark Christian festivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The agape was a communal fellowship meal held by early Christians and later revived by Methodists.

clue.text: Herb to accompany beef or fowl

indicators.note: to accompany means to go along with, so one piece sits right beside the other

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
to beef is to complain, as is to grouse

explanation.surface: A herb to serve with beef, or else with poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat for the kitchen but is a verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: This large game bird of the North American sagebrush plains is a kind of wild bird hunted for the table.

clue.text: Ammunition factory keeping officer's head dry in rain

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the rain word holds the other letters
in places the abstainer and the officer's letter inside the rain word

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain
TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays dry, avoiding alcohol

indicators.note: the head of the word officer's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A munitions works keeps its manager's head dry during a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Molten lead was dropped from the top of such a tall building into water to form round pellets; 'keeping ... in' wraps the rain round the teetotaller and the officer's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall building made lead pellets by dropping molten metal into water, so it manufactured ammunition.

clue.text: One taken round shop briefly

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the combined letters read in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
led means taken somewhere, guided

explanation.surface: One person escorted around the shop for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns ILED around; 'briefly' makes the definition a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for delicatessen, a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Bungled porn raid marks start of downfall?

indicators.note: a bungled job is botched, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A botched police raid on pornographers signals the beginning of their ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: A downfall is also a downpour, which begins with a single drop; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall can be a heavy fall of rain, and the first drop of water heralds one.

clue.text: Musical instrument used by top bloke making regular appearances

indicators.note: making regular appearances means only every other letter of top bloke shows up

explanation.surface: An instrument is played by a leading man who turns up at set intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of TOPBLOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind, a standard member of the orchestra.

clue.text: Weapon rejected by a politician in control

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the weapon's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A firearm is turned down by a politician who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes bodies or rules concerned with controlling, governing or overseeing an activity.

clue.text: Return to renew subscription

definitions.meaning: to answer back, reply or retort
to become a member of a club or society again

explanation.surface: A member goes back to renew a lapsed subscription.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean to retort, and also to become a member again of a club one had left.

clue.text: See me absorbed by less original verse

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so me goes inside the word for less original

parts.note: triter means more trite, so more hackneyed and less original

explanation.surface: Come and see me, soaked up in derivative poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word inviting you to look at what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of poetry with three metrical feet, and so a form of verse.

clue.text: Awareness of spiritual mysteries is evident in hymn, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means as seen in a mirror, so the whole is read backwards
evident in means showing up inside, so the word is sits within the hymn

parts.note: a hymn is a song of praise

explanation.surface: Spiritual knowledge shows itself in a hymn when one stops to reflect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident in' puts the short word inside the hymn, then 'on reflection' turns the whole thing round, giving SISONG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric insight into divine truths, the knowledge prized by the ancient Gnostics.

clue.text: Appropriate heavy metal sounds

indicators.note: sounds means the word is spoken, so the letters written are those of its soundalike

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself, to steal

explanation.surface: Fitting noise from a head-banging rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective, fitting, but is a verb; 'heavy metal' suggests rock music but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This iron-carbon alloy is a dense, hard material; the rock-music sense of heavy metal is the misdirection.

clue.text: Top white collar union

definitions.meaning: the highest point, summit or peak
a former British trade union for professional, executive and clerical staff

explanation.surface: The leading union for office workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The union was the Association of Professional, Executive, Clerical and Computer Staff, which merged into the GMB in 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: Means the highest point, and was also the acronym of a British trade union for clerical and professional staff.

clue.text: Gaffer assigned to cowboy film said to have horse in place

indicators.note: assigned to means attached to, so the boss's piece is joined on after the film's
said means spoken, so the film word is replaced by its soundalike

parts.note: a cowboy film is a western
gaffer is British slang for boss; super is short for superintendent
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A film boss is put on a western, with a horse on set somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: On a film set a gaffer is the chief electrician, but here it is simply a boss. The answer is a seaside resort in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort town on the Bristol Channel in Somerset, England, so a location.

clue.text: Queen and knight accompanied to the station

parts.note: a rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A queen and her knight were escorted to the police station.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone in is to arrest them and take them to a police station.

clue.text: It initially supports application to court by divorcee

indicators.note: by means beside, so the divorcee's piece sits next to the court application
initially picks out the first letter of the word supports

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
an appeal is an application to a higher court

explanation.surface: Something at first underpins a divorced person's petition to the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun but is the definition: old slang, made famous by Clara Bow, the It Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for magnetic physical allure, popularised by Clara Bow's 1927 film.
